title: $p^*$ preserves tensor products
statement:
For condensed abelian groups $F$ and $G$, the oplax tensor comparison
morphism $p^*(F\otimes G)\to p^*F\otimes p^*G$ of $p^*$ (for the oplax
structure of [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-unit] and the tensor products of
[sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]) is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the small-site and larger-value-universe convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $\mathcal C=*_{\mathrm{proét}}$, the profinite site of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and $\mathcal D=(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z)_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Take $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ to be [def-sfb-profinite-to-proetale]. The category of profinite sets has finite limits: its terminal object is a point, finite products are the topological products, and equalizers are the closed subspaces where the two maps agree, with their induced profinite topologies. The functor $u$ preserves these limits by [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-finite-limits], and it sends coverings to coverings by [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-cover-preserving], including the empty cover of the empty object. These are precisely the size, finite-limit and covering hypotheses of the general inverse-image theorem used in step 2.

source.place: Tag 00X6, proposition-get-morphism (hypotheses); the specialized functor and hypotheses are in main-20261015 sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point, clause 1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] to the sites and $u$ of step 1, taking only its geometric-morphism and abelian inverse-image clauses. The inverse image is left Kan extension along $u^{op}$ followed by sheafification, hence the specified $p^*$ of [def-sfb-point-upper-star], and the direct image is restriction, hence $p_*$ of [def-sfb-point-lower-star]. Thus they form a morphism of sites with finite-limit-preserving set inverse image. The convention in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], clause (3), identifies the abelian inverse image on underlying sets and its unit with the set inverse image and unit. We use exactly the Kan-extension/sheafification adjunction of [def-sfb-point-adjunction], not an independently chosen adjunction on the same functors. Consequently the bilinear-adjunction statement cited in step 3 applies to these particular functors and unit. No tensor comparison from the generic theorem is selected or assigned a normalization.

source.place: Tag 00X6, proposition-get-morphism; Section 00YR and Proposition 00YV(2) for the induced abelian inverse image and its underlying unit.

proof.text:
Use the set inverse image $L=p^*$ and direct image $R=p_*$ from step 2. The statement [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] identifies the induced abelian functors and their units with these underlying set functors and units. Apply [lem-sfb-site-inverse-image-bilinear-adjunction] to these particular functors: for abelian sheaves $F,G$ on the profinite site and $H$ on the pro-étale site it gives the bijection
$$\operatorname{Bilin}(p^*F\times p^*G,H)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Bilin}(F\times G,p_*H),\qquad\beta\longmapsto p_*\beta\circ(\eta_F\times\eta_G).$$
The finite-limit hypothesis is supplied by step 2. Here $\eta$ is the unit of the specified Kan-extension/sheafification adjunction. The cited lemma asserts both separate additivity and the displayed two-unit formula; we take precisely these clauses of its statement.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, third equality in the Hom/bilinear chain, specialized to integer-module sheaves; the exact two-unit formula is supplied by the cited bilinear-adjunction node.

proof.text:
Fix $F,G$ and put $A=p^*(F\otimes G)$ and $B=p^*F\otimes p^*G$. For any abelian sheaf $H$ on $(\Spec\mathbf Z)_{\mathrm{proét}}$, combine the bilinear bijection supplied in step 3 with the tensor universal property to obtain bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(B,H)\cong\operatorname{Bilin}(p^*F\times p^*G,H)\cong\operatorname{Bilin}(F\times G,p_*H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F\otimes G,p_*H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,H).$$
Here the tensor universal property follows directly from [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]: sectionwise integer-bilinear maps uniquely factor through the objectwise $\mathbf Z$-tensor, and the resulting natural map to a sheaf factors uniquely through its sheafification. Conversely precomposition with the pure-tensor maps recovers the bilinear family, so these operations are inverse. This uses the ordinary abelian-group tensor universal property, not any claim that all sections of a tensor sheaf are globally pure tensors. The last bijection is [def-sfb-point-adjunction]. Denote the composite by $\Psi_H$. By the formula in step 3 and the restriction formula of [def-sfb-point-lower-star], $\Psi_H(h)$ is the adjoint of the unique map $r_h:F\otimes G\to p_*H$ satisfying
$$ (r_h)_S(x\otimes y)=h_{u(S)}\bigl(\eta_F(x)\otimes\eta_G(y)\bigr) $$
for all profinite $S$ and $x\in F(S),y\in G(S)$, where tensors in sections mean their images in the tensor sheaf. In particular $\Psi_H$ is bijective with this precise formula.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, Hom/bilinear-adjunction chain; section-tensor-product (Tag 03EK), universal property preceding the lemma.

proof.text:
Let $\delta:A\to B$ be the oplax tensor comparison specified in [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-unit]. Write $\mu_{K,L}:p_*K\otimes p_*L\to p_*(K\otimes L)$ for the canonical lax comparison of restriction. From [def-sfb-point-lower-star] and the sheafified sectionwise tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], $\mu$ sends $x\otimes y$ at $S$ to the image of $x\otimes y$ at $u(S)$: this sectionwise bilinear family uniquely extends through the tensor and its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The defining formula for the left-adjoint oplax structure says that the adjoint of $\delta$ under [def-sfb-point-adjunction] is
$$d=\mu_{p^*F,p^*G}\circ(\eta_F\otimes\eta_G):F\otimes G\longrightarrow p_*B.$$
Therefore $d_S(x\otimes y)=\eta_F(x)\otimes\eta_G(y)$. For $h:B\to H$, the adjoint of $h\circ\delta$ is $p_*h\circ d$, which has exactly the formula for $r_h$ in step 4. The equality holds on the objectwise tensor presheaf by bilinearity, then on its sheafification by uniqueness. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection now gives $\Psi_H(h)=h\circ\delta$. Hence precomposition with the particular map $\delta$ is bijective for every $H$. This establishes the specified oplax map directly, without identifying it with an unnamed canonical isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, bilinear and adjunction formulas. The defining oplax-mate formula is Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Functor.lean:1064-1066, leftAdjointOplaxMonoidal; exact master Basic.lean:251-265 specifies this structure.

proof.text: Apply the surjectivity from step 5 with $H=A$: there is $e:B\to A$ with $e\circ\delta=\operatorname{id}_A$. Apply injectivity with $H=B$. Since $(\delta\circ e)\circ\delta=\delta\circ(e\circ\delta)=\delta=\operatorname{id}_B\circ\delta$, it gives $\delta\circ e=\operatorname{id}_B$. Thus $e$ is a two-sided inverse to $\delta$, proving the item.
